how.title: How to resize an image online

steps.title: Add your images
steps.text: Drag photos onto the page, choose them from your device or paste them. You can add as many as you like at once.

steps.title: Choose a size
steps.text: Pick a preset such as Instagram or passport photo, or enter your own width and height in pixels, centimeters, millimeters or inches. You can also set a maximum file size, for example 50 KB.

steps.title: Resize and download
steps.text: Press Resize images. Download each picture on its own or get everything in a single ZIP file.

items.title: Private by design
items.text: Your pictures are processed inside your browser. They are never uploaded to a server, so nobody else can see them.

items.title: Free and unlimited
items.text: No account, no watermark, no daily limit and no waiting. Resize one picture or hundreds.

items.title: Sharp results
items.text: A high-quality resizing filter and modern compressors keep small pictures clear and files small.

items.title: Exact file sizes
items.text: Need a photo under 50 KB for a form? Set the limit and the tool finds the best quality that fits.

items.q: Is it really free?
items.a: Yes. There is no sign-up, no trial and no daily limit. The site is paid for by a single advertisement next to the tool. Very large pictures can be too much for a phone or an old computer, and you will see a message if that happens.

items.q: Are my images uploaded?
items.a: No. Resizing happens on your own device, inside your browser. Your images are never sent to our servers.

items.q: Which formats are supported?
items.a: You can open JPG, PNG, WebP, GIF and BMP files, and AVIF where your browser supports it. You can save as JPG, PNG or WebP.

items.q: Will resizing reduce the quality?
items.a: Making a picture smaller keeps it sharp because the tool uses a high-quality filter. Making it larger cannot add detail that is not there, so enlarged pictures look softer. For JPG and WebP you can choose the quality yourself.

items.q: How do I get an image under a size such as 50 KB?
items.a: Turn on Limit the file size, type the number and press Resize images. The tool lowers the quality and, if needed, the dimensions until the file fits. Choose JPG or WebP for the best results, because PNG cannot be reduced that way.

items.q: Does it work on my phone?
items.a: Yes. The page works in current versions of Chrome, Safari, Firefox and Edge on phones, tablets and computers. Very large photos can be limited on older phones.

kb.title: Resize Image to 20KB, 50KB, 100KB or 200KB - Free
kb.description: Reduce a photo to an exact file size in KB for forms and uploads. Free, no signup, and your image stays on your device.
kb.h1: Resize image to KB (20 KB, 50 KB, 100 KB, 200 KB)
kb.intro: Many online forms, exam portals and job sites reject photos above a size limit such as 50 KB or 200 KB. This tool shrinks your image to fit the limit you choose while keeping as much quality as possible.

steps.title: Add your photo
steps.text: Drag it onto the page or choose it from your device.

steps.title: Set the size limit
steps.text: Pick a limit from the Preset list, or turn on Limit the file size and type your own number.

steps.title: Resize and download
steps.text: Press Resize images and download the result.

tips: Use JPG. It compresses photos much better than PNG at the same dimensions.
If the result looks blurry, raise the limit a little or crop away empty edges before resizing.
Some portals count 1 KB as 1,000 bytes and some as 1,024. This tool stays under the smaller number, so your file passes either way.
Check the required dimensions as well. Some portals need both a size in pixels and a limit in KB.

items.q: Why is my file still bigger than the limit?
items.a: Very detailed photos need more data. If the limit cannot be met even at the lowest quality, the tool also makes the picture smaller. If it still cannot reach the target, it tells you the smallest size it could make.

items.q: Can I resize many photos to the same limit?
items.a: Yes. Add all of them, set the limit once and download them together as a ZIP file.

items.q: Is my photo uploaded to a server?
items.a: No. Everything happens in your browser, so your photo never leaves your device.

cm.title: Resize Image in cm, mm or Inches - Free Online
cm.description: Set the exact size of a photo in centimeters, millimeters or inches with the right DPI. Free and private.
cm.h1: Resize image in cm, mm or inches
cm.intro: Printing and official forms often ask for a size in centimeters or inches instead of pixels. Enter the size and the DPI, and the tool works out the pixels for you.

steps.title: Add your photo
steps.text: Drag it onto the page or choose it from your device.

steps.title: Enter the size
steps.text: Choose cm, mm or in, then type the width and height. Use 300 DPI for good print quality.

steps.title: Resize and download
steps.text: Press Resize images and download the result.

tips: DPI means dots per inch. At 300 DPI, a picture that is 10 cm wide is about 1,181 pixels wide.
Use 300 DPI for prints and 72 to 96 DPI for screens.
Keep Lock aspect ratio on to avoid stretching. Turn it off and choose Crop to fill if you need an exact shape.
On a website only the pixel size matters. DPI matters when a picture is printed.

items.q: How many pixels is one inch?
items.a: It depends on the DPI. At 300 DPI one inch is 300 pixels. At 96 DPI it is 96 pixels.

items.q: Will it print at exactly this size?
items.a: The tool sets the pixel size that matches your size at the DPI you choose. Print the picture at its actual size, or at that DPI, to get the size you asked for.

items.q: What size is a 4 x 6 inch photo?
items.a: At 300 DPI, 4 x 6 inches is 1,200 x 1,800 pixels.

passport.title: Passport and Visa Photo Size by Country - Resize Free
passport.description: Common passport and visa photo sizes in mm, inches and pixels, with a free tool to resize your photo to match.
passport.intro: Different countries ask for different photo sizes. Pick your country in the Preset list to crop and resize your photo to the exact dimensions at 300 DPI.
passport.note: Rules change, and every application can add its own requirements such as background color, head size or no glasses. Always check the official instructions before you submit. This tool only sets the size; it does not check head size or background.

steps.title: Choose your size
steps.text: Open the Preset list, go to Photo ID and visa and pick your country.

steps.title: Add a photo
steps.text: Use a picture where your face is centered and clearly visible, because the tool crops from the middle.

steps.title: Resize and download
steps.text: Press Resize images. The picture is cropped to the required shape and saved as a JPG.

tips: Use a plain light background and even lighting without shadows.
Face the camera straight on and keep your face centered before you resize.
For online uploads, check the file size limit too and use Limit the file size.
Print at actual size (100 percent) so the paper size matches the requirement.

items.q: What is the standard passport photo size?
items.a: It varies. The United States uses 2 x 2 inches (51 x 51 mm). The United Kingdom, the European Union and Australia use 35 x 45 mm. Canada uses 50 x 70 mm.

items.q: Can I use this for a visa photo?
items.a: Yes, if the visa requirement matches one of the sizes. Many visas use the same size as the passport, but some countries have their own, so always check the official rules.

items.q: How many pixels is a passport photo?
items.a: At 300 DPI, 35 x 45 mm is 413 x 531 pixels and 2 x 2 inches is 600 x 600 pixels.

social.title: Social Media Image Sizes for Instagram, YouTube, Facebook
social.description: Widely used image sizes for Instagram, Facebook, YouTube, X, LinkedIn and Pinterest, plus a free tool to resize your picture to fit.
social.intro: Posts look best when the picture already has the right shape. Choose a platform in the Preset list and the tool crops and resizes your image to match.
social.note: Platforms update their recommendations from time to time. These are widely used sizes that work well with the current formats.

steps.title: Add your picture
steps.text: Drag it onto the page or choose it from your device.

steps.title: Choose a platform size
steps.text: Open the Preset list, go to Social media and pick the platform and format.

steps.title: Resize and download
steps.text: Press Resize images. Crop to fill is selected, so nothing is stretched.

tips: Keep important content away from the edges, because some apps trim the borders.
Use JPG or WebP for photos and PNG for graphics with sharp text.
Start from a picture larger than the target size for the best sharpness.

items.q: What is the best size for an Instagram post?
items.a: Use 1080 x 1080 pixels for a square post and 1080 x 1350 pixels for a portrait post.

items.q: What size should a YouTube thumbnail be?
items.a: 1280 x 720 pixels, with a file size below 2 MB.

items.q: Will my picture be cropped?
items.a: With Crop to fill the middle of the picture is kept and the edges that do not fit are trimmed. Choose Fit inside the box if you prefer to keep everything.

convert.title: Convert JPG, PNG and WebP Images - Free Online Converter
convert.description: Convert images between JPG, PNG and WebP in your browser. Free, no signup, and private.
convert.h1: Convert images between JPG, PNG and WebP
convert.intro: Choose the format you need and the tool converts every image you add. Nothing is uploaded.

steps.title: Add your images
steps.text: Add one or many pictures.

steps.title: Choose the format
steps.text: Select JPG, PNG or WebP under Format. Keep Keep size selected if you only want to change the format.

steps.title: Convert and download
steps.text: Press Resize images and download the results.

tips: JPG is best for photos. Files are small, but there is no transparency.
PNG is best for logos, screenshots and graphics with sharp edges or transparency. Files are larger.
WebP is a modern format that is usually smaller than JPG or PNG and works in all current browsers.
Converting a transparent PNG to JPG fills the see-through areas with white.

items.q: Does converting reduce the quality?
items.a: PNG output is lossless. JPG and WebP are lossy, but at high quality the difference is hard to see. You can set the quality yourself.

items.q: Can I convert HEIC photos from my iPhone?
items.a: Not yet, because most browsers cannot open HEIC files. On your iPhone you can set Camera formats to Most Compatible, or share the photo as a JPG.

compress.title: Compress Image Online - Reduce Photo Size Free
compress.description: Make photos smaller without losing visible quality. Free, no signup, and your images never leave your device.
compress.intro: Smaller images load faster, fit in emails and save storage. The tool re-encodes your pictures with modern compressors and lets you set a quality level or a maximum file size.

steps.title: Add your images
steps.text: Drag them onto the page or choose them from your device.

steps.title: Choose how to compress
steps.text: Keep Keep size to compress without changing the dimensions and use the Quality slider, or turn on Limit the file size.

steps.title: Compress and download
steps.text: Press Resize images and download the results.

tips: A quality of 70 to 85 is usually enough for photos and cuts the size a lot.
Reducing the dimensions shrinks a file far more than lowering the quality alone.
WebP files are usually smaller than JPG for the same look.
Photos from phones contain hidden data such as location. Files made here do not.

items.q: How much smaller will my file be?
items.a: Photos straight from a phone often shrink by 60 to 90 percent. Pictures that are already compressed shrink less.

items.q: Can I compress many images at once?
items.a: Yes. Add them all and download a single ZIP file.
